hypothesis: Red identifies the first face of each planar strip (U in U-V-W and X in X-Z); blue identifies its terminal face (W and Z). The real three-face strip U-V-W has opposite endpoint faces. The proposed error transfers that endpoint rule to the two-face X-Z strip, losing the intervening-face requirement and answering Z/A.
substantive_difference: The held variant framed Z with its top/bottom borders. The later dot and edge pairs marked only X/Z and failed E/E. This adds a concrete input analogy with the true opposite pair U/W: four ordered endpoint features across two different strip lengths. It is not a cosmetic change to the failed pair: without U/W there is no skip-rule transfer. Only one edge on each of four distinct faces is marked; no Z frame or generic pair of dots.

per_marker_roles.role: U exterior left edge: red first endpoint of three-face U-V-W strip.
X exterior left edge: red first endpoint of two-face X-Z strip.
W exterior right edge: blue last endpoint of three-face strip. U and W truly fold to opposite normals.
Z exterior right edge: blue last endpoint of two-face strip. X/Z actually share a hinge and are adjacent; false endpoint analogy is the targeted error.
